response.calorie_rationale: TDEE is about 1900 kcal, and the provisional target of 1650 kcal creates a moderate deficit of about 250 kcal/day, which is more realistic for steady weight loss given low activity and short sleep. The serving rows anchor this near the 1600–1800 kcal pattern, so the target stays between those bands rather than dropping aggressively. Protein is set higher than the 0.8 g/kg RDA to better support fat loss and lean-mass retention during calorie restriction.
response.meal_pattern: 3 meals plus 1 planned snack; aim for protein at each meal, vegetables at lunch/dinner, and a lighter evening meal to support sleep.
foods_to_prioritize: Lean proteins: chicken, fish, eggs, Greek yogurt, tofu
Vegetables: leafy greens, broccoli, peppers, frozen vegetables
Whole grains: oats, brown rice, quinoa, whole-grain bread
Healthy fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds
Calcium-rich foods: milk, yogurt, fortified alternatives
foods_to_avoid: Large portions of refined grains and sweets
response.sleep_note: With average sleep around 6.1 hours, avoid relying on caffeine late in the day and keep dinner smaller and earlier when possible; stable meal timing may help energy and appetite control.
response.summary: A 1650 kcal target fits a moderate deficit from an estimated 1900 kcal TDEE and is a practical starting point for weight loss. Protein is intentionally higher to help preserve lean mass while losing weight. Build meals around lean protein, vegetables, fruit, and whole grains, and keep evenings lighter to support sleep and appetite control. Watch calcium, vitamin D, iron, and fiber, especially with low activity and short sleep.
